summary: H.R. 9899, the Afghanistan TPS Act of 2026, designates Afghanistan for Temporary Protected Status (TPS) under the Immigration and Nationality Act. This allows eligible nationals of Afghanistan living in the United States to apply for TPS and employment authorization through July 1, 2029.

affected_groups.effect: Eligible to apply for Temporary Protected Status, employment authorization, fee waivers, and emergency travel authorization if they meet physical presence, admissibility, and background check requirements.
affected_groups.group: Nationals of Afghanistan in the United States

affected_groups.effect: Required to process and adjudicate applications within specified timelines and handle fee waiver and travel authorization requests.

key_provisions: Designates Afghanistan for Temporary Protected Status beginning on the date of the Act's enactment through July 1, 2029.

Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to receive, process, and adjudicate TPS and employment authorization applications from Afghan nationals within 90 days, with a potential 150-day extension for national security reasons.
Sets eligibility criteria requiring Afghan nationals to have been continuously physically present in the U.S. since the enactment date, be admissible, and complete background checks.
Allows the Secretary of Homeland Security to grant prior consent for temporary travel abroad to TPS holders under emergency and extenuating circumstances.
Permits applicants who are only eligible due to this Act to apply for a waiver of fees associated with the TPS application.
missing_information: The exact number of Afghan nationals who will be eligible for or receive Temporary Protected Status under this bill.
The financial cost of processing applications and waiving fees.

summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes statutory Temporary Protected Status for nationals of Afghanistan through July 1, 2029, altering immigration processes and requirements for this group within the United States.
